title: Trillion Ligands per Day: Performance-Portable Virtual Screening via Compound Database Optimization and Multi-Target Docking
problem: Structure-based virtual screening for drug discovery must scale to trillion-ligand libraries, but current methods lack the computational efficiency and portability for extreme-scale screening across multiple protein targets.
motivation: Drug discovery is bottlenecked by the ability to screen massive ligand libraries against multiple protein targets. Existing approaches cannot achieve the throughput needed for modern drug development at petascale. Performance portability is critical for diverse HPC systems.
method: SWDOCKP2 works by first organizing the molecule database—grouping similar molecular shapes through conformational sorting and merging—to enable faster screening. It then aligns search grids for multiple protein targets and screens them in parallel, testing many targets simultaneously rather than sequentially. To accelerate the core calculations, it uses SIMD (single-instruction multiple-data, where a processor performs the same operation on many data points at once) to speed up trilinear interpolation, a mathematical technique for estimating values between known points. Finally, it uses an emulator for the Sunway processor architecture, allowing the code to run efficiently across different hardware platforms.
key_novelty: The core idea is organizing the molecule database by conformational shape and screening multiple protein targets in parallel, enabling trillion-ligand drug screening.
contributions: Ligand database optimization with conformational sorting and merging
Multi-receptor grid alignment for parallel screening
Sunway architecture emulator for cross-platform design
1.9 trillion ligand-receptor pairs/day on Sunway OceanLight (39M cores)
Unprecedented protein-ligand interaction dataset for ML
limitations: Specific optimization for Sunway architecture; conformational sampling may affect accuracy; scaling requires massive parallel resources.
